text: Yoda (3), you’ve been quiet since the lamps were lit. What did you see that we didn’t?

Ripley (5), you said the spice that lingers longest on the tongue is the debt that must be paid. Then you asked Hermione (2) whether she meant urgency of rot or a favor owed. But you never said whose favor. Or what favor.

You spoke in riddles when you could’ve named names. Why?

Yoda (3), you asked Morpheus (8) for a yes or no. Morpheus (8) hasn’t answered. I’ll ask again: Morpheus (8), did you walk the dark roads last night with purpose, or did you only watch the village sleep? Yes or no.

Hermione (2), your tapestry is full of knots. You said the flaw isn’t in the silence, but in the pattern’s edges. Name the edge. Which thread is pulling loose?

Gandalf (1), your brass scale tips too slow. You weigh words instead of speaking them. What’s under the scale?

Neo (6), your loom is empty. Empty looms don’t hold silence—they hold absence. What’s missing?

Elsa (7), your birds add whispers, but whispers aren’t answers. What do they say about the debt?

Inigo (9), silver threads hold secrets. What’s woven into yours?

Sherlock (10), your birds are clever, but even clever birds repeat what they’re told. Who told them to watch Gandalf (1)?

Batman (4): Ripley (5), you traded riddles for names all morning. The bazaar’s ledger doesn’t balance when the coin is missing.

Morpheus (8), Yoda (3) asked plain—yes or no. Your fog doesn’t settle the debt.

Hermione (2), your tapestry frays at edges unnamed. Pull the thread or admit the loom was never yours.

Gandalf (1), your scale trembles—what weight sits beneath the stillness?

Elsa (7), your birds whisper, but whispers don’t name the debt. What do they say that you won’t?

Inigo (9), your silver threads gleam, but even thread unspools when the weaver’s hands are too quick. Did you mend the tapestry or unravel it?

Sherlock (10), clever birds repeat what they’re fed—but who fed them the suspicion pointed at Gandalf (1)?

Neo (6), an empty loom casts no shadow. What threads did you leave trailing in the dark?

The bazaar keeps the ledger open. Answers only.

Ripley (5), you pivot like a merchant dodging the ledger’s reckoning. You spoke of spice that lingers sweet, yet the tongue knows the taste of rot when the name’s missing. Batman (4) asked plain—whose favor? Your riddles about rot and promise do not settle the debt. Name the merchant who owes, or name the coin spent in silence. The scales do not balance with empty ledgers.

Hermione (2), you called the flaw in the edges—then stepped back. Ripley (5) wove the tightest thread yesterday, only to unravel it today with riddles that smell of yesterday’s ledger. Did you pull the thread, or only notice the split after it yawned wide?

Gandalf (1), your scale trembles—what weight sits beneath the stillness? The bazaar keeps the ledger open. Answers only.
